answer: In sponsor-collateral lineage, a new identity may only join under a member who escrows part of its standing as bond; its attestations must be countersigned by that sponsor, so cost travels down the chain instead of appearing from nowhere. A ring whose clones co-vote in lockstep is easy to fingerprint, and on convergence the upstream branch is slashed. Attackers pay twice: to buy bonded sponsors, then in destroyed reputation when the pattern surfaces. Standing is quartz-hard, the bond has copper weight, lotus-cheap keys buy nothing alone. Branching factor, not node count, is capped.
